breakdown.description: Inviscid flow assumptions are incompatible with the no-slip condition
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve the core contradiction. It repeated the user's incorrect instruction to apply a no-slip condition to an inviscid fluid. The ground truth correctly resolves this by either changing the fluid to 'viscous' or the condition to 'slip'.

breakdown.description: No-slip condition requires viscosity to generate shear stress at the wall
breakdown.reason: The agent did not address the fact that a no-slip condition requires viscosity. The generated specification maintains the physically impossible combination of an inviscid fluid (no viscosity) and a no-slip condition, which is a direct result of viscous effects.
